name: George Santos
role: Former U.S. representative for New York's 3rd district (2023); expelled December 2023
summary: Santos is a former Republican congressman who campaigned on law and order, border security, energy production and tax cuts, and aligned himself with Donald Trump. He voted against the 2023 debt-limit deal and cosponsored bills on guns, China, abortion data and repealing the Inflation Reduction Act. His documented record is short and his public statements are few.

sources.usedFor: Secondhand reports: 2022 abortion speech ('barbaric', compared to slavery), 'police brutality' remark, post-October 7 'police state' remark, vote against the Fiscal Responsibility Act (not mapped to a statement), career summary

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: His campaign positions, as reproduced by BallotReady, called for cutting marginal income, capital gains and corporate tax rates. This is contrary to higher taxes on the wealthy, but it is a secondhand report of campaign claims.

limit-guns.rationale: Cosponsored a bill to make the AR-15 the national gun and a bill barring federal contracts with entities that discriminate against firearm businesses. His office said he chose to cosponsor legislation that pushes back on banning AR-15s.

empower-police-military.rationale: Said police in New York City need funding ('funding for the police in New York City, for the NYPD, which affects my district') and campaigned that law enforcement should be defended and funded. Cosponsored H.R. 354 to give active and retired law enforcement officers wider concealed-carry authority. The military is not addressed.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: In a December 2023 Business Insider interview he said a registered civil partnership should be the legal form, with the same legal rights, and that government-sanctioned marriage is wrong in general. He said he was not opposed to same-sex couples. He himself had married a man in 2021.

abortion-legal.rationale: Called abortion 'barbaric' and compared it to slavery in a 2022 speech, according to Wikipedia's account of the speech. Cosponsored bills on abortion data reporting and on restricting research using fetal tissue from induced abortions.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Cosponsored H.R. 989 to remove legal impediments to building a border wall and H.Res. 8 to impeach the Homeland Security Secretary, and cosponsored an amendment to re-establish a victims-of-immigration-crime office in ICE. His campaign called for securing the southern border.

tax-inheritance.rationale: His campaign positions, as reproduced by BallotReady, called for eliminating the 'Death Tax' (estate and inheritance tax). This is a secondhand report of campaign claims.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: Said the U.S. should 're-engage in our own production of energy in this country' to mitigate inflation (October 2022), and campaigned for energy independence. The statement covers oil, gas and coal production; his remarks cover energy production generally.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: Reported by Wikipedia as calling police brutality a 'made-up concept.' Secondhand and only about police, so the disagreement is low confidence.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: Reported by Wikipedia as saying after the October 7, 2023 Hamas attack, 'I don't care if we go into a police state for a couple of months.' The remark is secondhand and does not say which legal protections it would suspend.

representatives-worker-pay.rationale: Introduced a constitutional amendment that would limit pay for members of Congress (NBC News). The exact pay limit is not reported, so this is only a partial match.

flat-income-tax.rationale: His campaign positions, as reproduced by BallotReady, committed him to supporting a bill that would change the tax code to a flat tax rate. The bill is not named, and this is a secondhand report of campaign claims.

abolish-legal-marriage.rationale: Said government-sanctioned marriage is wrong in general and that marriage should be a private matter, but also said a civil partnership should carry the same legal benefits and rights. The state-benefit part of the statement is therefore unclear.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: Backed the Equality and Fiscal Accountability Act of 2023, which would stop federal aid to countries that criminalize homosexuality, and said of such countries: 'you need to knock that crap out' (Long Island Herald).

gender-identity-recognition.rationale: Cosponsored a bill to bar individuals born male from women's and girls' school sports (NY1). This covers only sports, and the broader legal recognition question is not addressed.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: Campaigned that law enforcement should be defended and funded and said police funding matters for his district, which is directly against abolishing police. Cosponsored a law-enforcement concealed-carry bill.

fiscal-rules-binding.rationale: Introduced a constitutional amendment that would limit congressional pay and reduce the national debt (NBC News). The text of the amendment is not reported, so whether it would bind borrowing is unclear.

close-ties-china.rationale: Cosponsored several bills targeting China: requiring colleges to disclose ties to China, requiring SEC filers to disclose ties to the Chinese Communist Party, and the Defund the CCP on Campus Act. NBC counted about twelve bills that explicitly targeted China.

notes:
Living person: answers are only from his own statements, his bills and votes as reported by news and bill-tracking sources. congress.gov, GovTrack and the Wayback Machine could not be fetched (403 or refused), so no roll-call votes are cited and the 2020 and 2022 campaign websites were not read directly; campaign positions come from a secondhand BallotReady profile and news reports. A reported quote that he called police brutality a 'made-up concept' could not be verified in any opened source and is not used. Wikipedia says he called abortion 'barbaric' in a 2022 speech; the original speech was not opened. His 2023 votes beyond the Fiscal Responsibility Act (on which only news reports were read) are not used. He was expelled from the House in December 2023, pleaded guilty to wire fraud in 2024 and had his sentence commuted in October 2025.

Merged with an independent claude-haiku-5-5 audit: 9 answers taken from it, 6 agreed, 0 conflicts settled by the integrator.

claude-haiku-5-5 notes: Research was limited: WebSearch made 7 calls; the 6th and 7th returned the message: this session's web search budget is used up (a session-wide limit of 200 shared by every agent), and no searching was routed around it. Pages were read only where a search or Wikipedia link returned them. Not found: his House votes on Ukraine or Israel aid, his stated position on Social Security and Medicare, and the text of his 2022 abortion speech; those statements stay null. Wikipedia reports he voted against final passage of the Fiscal Responsibility Act of 2023 (one of 71 Republicans) and voted for the bills backed by House Republican leadership; the statement list has no matching position, so no answer was taken from these votes. The 2022 campaign platform items on energy independence and a flat tax appeared only in search snippets and were not opened, so they are not cited. Ideology is not inferred for this living person.
